ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Rocky Marciano Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Establishing primary care after retirement from professional boxing: low back pain and left leg pain after a recent disc herniation, left thumb pain, weight gain and blood pressure after stopping training, a brain health baseline, mood, anxiety and sleep, and a sports medicine consultation. Concerns: Back and leg pain since bending to lift a child, and an old back ache, which stop him driving far or training; An aching left thumb when he grips or opens a jar; He has put on weight since he stopped training and wants to stay in shape and healthy for his family; He has read about boxers whose memory and speech fail later in life and wants to know his own state now. [S]

One tablet twice a day with food for two weeks, then as needed; no more than two tablets a day
Diclofenac sodium 1% gel, 2 g rubbed into the base of the left thumb up to four times a day
2 g to the base of the left thumb up to four times a day
Omeprazole 20 mg delayed-release capsule, one each morning before breakfast for four weeks
One capsule each morning, 30 minutes before breakfast, for four weeks

Hand-based thumb carpometacarpal orthosis (thumb spica splint) fitted, to wear during gripping work and at night
Physical therapy evaluation of the lumbar spine with a plan for directional preference exercise, motor control and progressive strengthening, twice a week for six weeks

list.item: Chronic mechanical low back pain for about seven years of heavy training and fighting, aching across the lower back, worse after long drives and in the morning: active, confirmed [S]

Lumbar disc herniation at L4-L5 with left L5 radiculopathy, a few weeks old and improving: sharp pain into the left buttock and calf after bending to lift a child at home, seen in a hospital emergency department, where MRI showed a left paracentral L4-L5 disc extrusion contacting the left L5 nerve root; leg pain now intermittent, with slight numbness over the top of the left foot and normal strength; no bladder or bowel change: active, confirmed [S]

Post-traumatic osteoarthritis of the left thumb base (first carpometacarpal joint) after an old fracture at the base of the first metacarpal from his early fighting years, with pain on pinching and gripping, an ache after long gripping, and a positive grind test: active, confirmed [S]
Overweight after retirement, with a weight gain of about 9 kg in the four months since he stopped training, eating as he did in training camp; BMI 28.7: active, confirmed [S]
Elevated blood pressure reading at intake (136/86 mmHg, average of two) without a diagnosis of hypertension; home readings to confirm: resolved, confirmed [S]

History of repetitive head impacts from about thirteen years of Army, amateur and professional boxing, including heavy sparring; no remembered loss of consciousness; normal brain health baseline (no cognitive, mood or behavioral complaints; MoCA 29); traumatic encephalopathy syndrome not suspected: active, confirmed [S]

Epigastric pain and burning for six days after about seven weeks of near-daily naproxen, worse at night and on an empty stomach; no vomiting, black stools, blood or weight loss; normal hemoglobin; no alarm features; NSAID-associated dyspepsia: resolved, confirmed [S]

tr.td: Establishing primary care after retirement from professional boxing: low back pain and left leg pain after a recent disc herniation, left thumb pain, weight gain and blood pressure after stopping training, a brain health baseline, mood, anxiety and sleep, and a sports medicine consultation
Two-week review on the day of the sports medicine consultation: back and leg pain, the thumb, home blood pressure, the brain health baseline and an exercise plan
Eight-week review: back pain after six weeks of physical therapy, the thumb splint, the stomach after stopping naproxen, weight and blood pressure
Twelve-week review: back and thumb on home programs, weight, blood pressure, mood, anxiety and sleep, and the plan ahead
Same-day sick visit for epigastric pain on naproxen

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Back and leg pain: neurological examination of the legs at every visit; red flags reviewed (new weakness, saddle numbness, bladder or bowel change, fever, weight loss) with instructions to come the same day if any appear; the outside MRI reviewed and no repeat imaging unless the deficit progresses; naproxen with food for two weeks then as needed; heat and staying active; no opioids, no muscle relaxants, no bed rest

Sports medicine consultation for the disc herniation and chronic back pain, the thumb base, a brain health baseline after repetitive head impacts, and an exercise prescription for life after heavy training
Physical therapy twice a week for six weeks (directional preference exercise, motor control and core strengthening), then a home program; a graded return to running and swimming
Thumb base: X-ray of the hand; topical diclofenac gel; hand-protection advice
Thumb orthosis for gripping work and at night, hand therapy exercises, and a corticosteroid injection only if pain persists

Weight and cardiovascular risk after heavy training: home blood pressure monitoring with a validated upper-arm cuff, twice a day for a week, before any diagnosis; a meal plan matched to his lower energy needs; lipids and HbA1c at intake; repeat risk assessment yearly
Exercise prescription: 150 to 300 minutes a week of moderate aerobic activity (walking, swimming and cycling, then running) and strength training twice a week, with no sparring or other head impacts

Brain health baseline after repetitive head impacts: symptom inventory (headache, memory, attention, mood, behavior, sleep, balance), MoCA, PHQ-9, GAD-7 and PROMIS sleep at intake; no brain imaging without an indication; repeat yearly; traumatic encephalopathy syndrome is a research diagnosis and is not made on history alone
Mood and anxiety: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and again at twelve weeks; support for the change of life after retirement
Stomach on NSAIDs: stop naproxen; omeprazole for four weeks; stool test for Helicobacter pylori; no further oral NSAIDs; topical diclofenac continued
Leg pain gone and back pain at 3 or less out of 10, with an Oswestry index under 20%
Back pain 6 to 3 out of 10 and Oswestry 36% to 18% at eight weeks; no leg pain
Grip and pinch without thumb pain at 3 or less out of 10
Thumb pain 5 to 2 out of 10; left grip 38 to 46 kg
Lose 5% to 7% of body weight over six months with regular exercise
Blood pressure under 120/80 mmHg at home without medicine
Home average 126/78 mmHg in the week after intake and 118/74 mmHg before the twelve-week visit; clinic 122/76
Keep a documented brain health baseline and repeat it yearly
MoCA 29, PHQ-9 3, GAD-7 4 and a normal symptom inventory at intake; repeat in a year
